name: VM5a
description: A six-layer radial viscosity profile, prescribed for GIAMIP experiments Exp01 and Exp06. It is a viscosity structure only: the elastic structure is PREM-stable (protocol v4.0 Section 3.1) and the rheology is Maxwell.

source.citation: Roy, K. and Peltier, W. R. (2017). Space-geodetic and water level gauge constraints on continental uplift and tilting over North America. Geophysical Journal International 210(2), 1115-1142, table 2. Reproduced in the GIAMIP protocol v4.0, section 3.2.1.

notes: The protocol tabulates viscosity in units of 1e21 Pa s. The values here are in Pa s.
The 100-420 km and 420-670 km layers carry the same viscosity, so the profile has five distinct values across six layers.
The protocol states that each group may choose its own treatment of compressibility.

Protocol v4.0 gives the deepest layer as reaching the core-mantle boundary. In PREM-stable that boundary is at a radius of 3480 km, a depth of 2891 km, so the deepest layer ends there. giamip.earth takes the boundary from the elastic structure.
